projects.name: Umeed
projects.type: Hope-Centred Mental Health First Aid Companion for Pakistan
projects.stack: Next.js • React • TypeScript • Node.js • Express • OpenRouter LLMs • Tailwind CSS
projects.summary: A mental health support companion that adapts to how each person says they want to cope: talking to family, seeing a professional, or coping on their own. It never guesses someone's culture from demographics. It pairs a warm conversational AI with a server-side crisis detector that doesn't depend on the AI's judgment, so someone in danger is never left inside a chat window.
highlights: Built a two-layer crisis safety net that runs on the server, alongside the AI rather than inside it. A pattern engine sorts messages into high-severity and warning language. A second AI classifier reads every message in parallel to catch indirect phrasings, and if that classifier ever fails, the message is treated as a crisis rather than ignored. When either layer triggers, the chat hands off to a full-screen "Safety Mode" with hotlines and a guided breathing exercise.

Designed for how Pakistanis actually text: a lightweight language detector tells apart English, Roman Urdu, Roman Punjabi and code-switched mixes ("yar I'm just not feeling good today"), and the companion replies in the same register. A carefully tuned system prompt forbids diagnosing anyone or claiming to replace therapy, and only adapts to preferences users state themselves.

projects.name: Terrarium
projects.type: Neighbourhood-Scale Climate Intervention Simulator for Lahore
projects.stack: Python • FastAPI • React • TypeScript • LightGBM • MapLibre
projects.summary: An interactive climate simulator letting city officers and residents test real interventions — planting trees, restricting traffic — on an actual 20km × 20km tile of Lahore at 100m resolution (40,602 cells), and see the modeled result rather than a vague estimate.
highlights: Built a three-layer architecture: a unified state cube merging satellite and population datasets into one aligned data cube; physics cores including a LightGBM model for surface temperature change, an FFT-based air dispersion model for PM2.5, and an equity core mapping cooling impact by population decile; and a FastAPI backend serving a React/MapLibre/deck.gl frontend for live visualization.

Supports natural-language plan input (e.g. “plant 5,000 trees here”), generates council-ready PDF briefs with uncertainty disclosure, and explicitly refuses infeasible interventions with the underlying arithmetic rather than silently approximating them.

Achieved a hindcast accuracy of 0.91–1.24°C mean absolute error with positive spatial skill after correcting for offset errors, and validated the air quality model against 53 independent monitoring stations.

projects.name: Research Paper Implementation
projects.stack: Python • TensorFlow/Keras • Deep Learning • LSTM • CNN
projects.summary: Two deep learning classifiers benchmarked against published research — an LSTM for human activity recognition and a VGG-16 CNN for image classification.
highlights: LSTM on UCI-HAR: 93.32% test accuracy (within 92–95% published benchmark range), 561 sensor features, 6 activity classes
VGG-16 on CIFAR-10 (from scratch): 88.38% Top-1 / 99.12% Top-5 accuracy, beating the original paper's Top-5 by 0.12%
Stacked LSTM (128→64 units) with dropout, Adam optimizer, sparse categorical cross-entropy
VGG-16 adapted for 32×32 input: reduced FC width (4096→512), batch norm after conv blocks, dropout at 0.25/0.5
Interesting finding: Sitting/Standing and Cat/Dog were the hardest class pairs, consistent with literature, showing analytical thinking beyond just running the model.
